Subject: Dedicated sizing: quick Q&A + sample traffic for BrightLedger

Hi Emma —

Great to meet you on the demo last week. To give you a fast, defensible sizing and cost estimate for a Dedicated deployment that meets your SLA, we need a few concrete traffic signals from BrightLedger. I attached a short PDF questionnaire (redwood_dedicated_questionnaire.pdf) — filling out the highlighted fields will let us map token velocity, concurrency, and burst tolerance to a preliminary GPU footprint.

Short asks (should only take ~10 minutes):
- Average prompt length and 95th percentile prompt length (tokens)
- Average response length and 95th percentile response length (tokens)
- Peak concurrent sessions and sustained concurrency during business hours
- Dayparting / burst windows (times and expected multiple over baseline)
- P95 latency SLO for user-facing flows
- Any KV-cache/prefix reuse (are users sending the same context repeatedly?)
- Whether batchable background/async inference is possible for parts of the workload

If you prefer, drop the raw sample CSV of recent traffic and we can extract the prompt/response histograms ourselves — that speeds things up.

I copied our pre-sales lead (Marissa), capacity engineer (Karthik), and Ben from account execs so we can turn this into a proposed commitment + burst plan quickly.

Next step: If you can send the completed questionnaire or a sample CSV by tomorrow, we’ll aim to get a first-pass Dedicated sizing (GPU types + burst pool recommendation) within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: quick Q&A + sample traffic for BrightLedger

Laura —

Thanks, attached is a small export (traffic_sample.csv) and answers inline below. Samir is on copy. Let me know if we need more detail.

Answers (high level):
- Average prompt length: ~38 tokens (p95 prompt: 120 tokens)
- Average response length: ~310 tokens (p95 response: 1,200 tokens)
- Peak concurrent sessions (observed): 120 concurrent queries during end-of-day reconciliation windows; typical sustained concurrency during business hours: 35–50
- Dayparting/burst: big spikes at 17:30–18:15 UTC and smaller spikes at 00:00–00:30 UTC; spikes can be ~6–8x baseline for ~20 minutes
- P95 latency SLO: 800ms for interactive flows; background jobs can tolerate 2–5s
- KV/prefix reuse: moderate — many requests include a persistent customer profile blob (~1–2KB) that repeats across calls for a given session
- Batchable background: yes — reconciliation jobs are batchable and can be scheduled off-peak

Notes: we attached the CSV with 24 hours of anonymized request records (timestamp,prompt_tokens,response_tokens,session_id,route). Hope that helps.

—Emma

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you run a back-of-envelope GPU footprint (A100-equivalent GPUs) for an SLO of 800ms p95 given the token mix and the 6–8x 20-minute bursts? Include recommended burst pool sizing and whether KV cache would materially reduce steady-state GPU needs.
- Marissa/Ben: confirm if BrightLedger is within our typical committed tiers or if we should propose a custom reserved fleet (deal id BL-2025-098).
- Irene: any red flags on security/data residency from the CSV? (it is anonymized but note their region is US-based)

I want a short slide we can share with the customer by EOD tomorrow: recommended GPU count (steady + burst), suggested QoS routing (interactive vs batch), and estimated monthly committed cost ballpark.

Thanks — Laura

Laura / team — quick first-pass sizing notes after a brief run on the CSV and token-mixing heuristics. Keeping this high level for the slide: 

Summary recommendation (first pass) — interactive SLO 800ms p95
- Steady-state: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed 40–45 tps aggregate given avg token lengths and typical batching)
- Burst pool: +3 GPUs (to handle 6–8x for 20m windows) with autoscaling policy to add GPUS for short windows; reserve warm slots for KV cache affinity
- If we enable aggressive KV prefix caching for the repeating 1–2KB customer blobs, we estimate ~15–20% reduction in steady-state GPU need (~1 GPU) and improved p95 tail
- For background reconciliation (batch), route to cheaper/scheduled instances (4x smaller nodes) to offload long responses and avoid driving interactive latency

Notes and caveats:
- p95 1.2k responses push token compute; if customers expect sustained p95 under 500ms we’d need materially more GPUs or a lower-latency model variant (quantized, lower flops).
- Suggest quantization to int8 for the model variant used in Dedicated to reduce GPU memory and increase packing; we can validate quality with a small eval set.
- Attachment: sla_matrix.xlsx — includes cost ballpark, estimated sustained vs burst vCPU/GPU hours, and suggested fallback policy (route to hosted smaller model if Dedicated capacity saturated).

Next steps: I can convert this into a 1-slide sizing & cost ballpark for the customer. If they accept, we should schedule a 30m call with BrightLedger to validate dayparting assumptions and confirm commit level.

—Karthik
